instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each legislative agent and each employer to file a statement of expenditures with the updated registration statement.
Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) are due by the last day of January, May, and September each year, i.e., three times annually.
Section 101.72(B) requires updated registration statements (with expenditures) to be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year.
The statute specifies three filings per year (January, May, September), not a single annual spending report cadence.
Quarterly filing (four times per year) is not provided; instead the statute sets three filing dates per year.
The statute requires filing three times annually, not twice per year.
No monthly filing requirement appears; filings are tied to January, May, and September updates.
The statute enumerates specific triannual due dates and does not provide an additional alternative cadence.
Legislative agents must report the total amount of expenditures made during the reporting period, and employers must also show their total expenditures.
When specified thresholds/conditions are met, the filer must disclose the recipient name, total amount, description, and approximate date for expenditures, which constitutes itemized reporting.
The expenditure statement requires per-recipient disclosure with dates, descriptions, and amounts for certain expenditures, reflecting an itemized format.
Expenditure is defined to include gifts and items such as food, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and §101.73 requires reporting expenditures to or for covered officials.
The expenditure statement must list the specific items of legislation (if any) for which expenditures were made, and updated registrations list specific bills or resolutions advocated.
Updated registration statements must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the period.
For reported expenditures, the filer must identify the specific items of legislation (if any) for which the expenditures were made, tying spending to an issue/bill.
The expenditure statement focuses on amounts, recipients, descriptions, dates, and legislation/client identifiers, and does not require reporting general subject matter categories.
No requirement appears to list general issues apart from identifying specific legislation (if any) connected to an expenditure.
Section 101.73 governs expenditure reporting and does not require disclosure of lobbying contacts made.
While the law requires listing specific bills/resolutions and linking expenditures to legislation, it does not require stating support/oppose position.

The statute expressly excludes 'compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of expenditures for employer statements and does not require reporting compensation totals in the spending report.
Compensation is excluded from employer expenditure reporting and no provision in §101.73 requires compensation to be reported by payer.
Office facility expenses are excluded from 'expenditures' for employer statements, indicating indirect costs are not required to be reported.
The expenditure statement must include 'the identity of the client on whose behalf each expenditure was made,' which identifies the principal/client.
Section 101.73 does not require listing any client/principal address or contact information, only identity of the client for each expenditure.
No requirement in the expenditure-statement section calls for describing the principal's business or nature of business.
The expenditure statement requirements in §101.73 do not include lobbyist name/address fields (those appear in registration under §101.72, not in the spending report content).
Expenditures are defined and reported as made to or for the benefit of specified public officers/employees, with no mention of household or family members as covered recipients.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text does not state whether a 'zero' (no expenditures) statement must still be filed; §101.73 requires filing a statement but is silent on no-activity/zero-report situations.
